name: TX-29
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Sylvia Garcia running with a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger has raised no money
model.rationale: Garcia holds a D+17 district, is a renominated incumbent, and has raised nearly $1 million with outside support while Fierro has raised nothing. Markets price her near certain, so the forecast stays at a roughly 24-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending against Garcia showing a closer race would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sylvia Garcia seeks another term in a Houston-area district that leans Democratic by about 17 points. She enters the general election as the renominated incumbent with roughly $1 million raised this cycle and more than $560,000 in outside support, while her cash position stands near $200,000.

Republican challenger Martha Fierro has reported no fundraising and no outside spending on either side. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Garcia's chances around 94 percent. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and a large financial imbalance makes this a Safe Democratic seat, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any specific sign of a competitive race.
